# convex_custom_domain (Resource)

Points a custom domain at a Convex deployment.

Convex verifies the domain asynchronously once its DNS records resolve. Creating this resource registers the domain and returns immediately, so a fresh domain is normally unverified: `verified` is `false` until the DNS is in place and Convex has checked it. Terraform does not wait for verification, and a later refresh is what picks it up.

Convex offers no endpoint for changing a custom domain, so every attribute forces replacement.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "convex_project" "app" {
  team_id = var.convex_team_id
  name    = "My Application"
}

resource "convex_deployment" "prod" {
  project_id      = convex_project.app.id
  deployment_type = "prod"
  is_default      = true
}

# Fronts the deployment's .convex.cloud API URL.
resource "convex_custom_domain" "api" {
  deployment_name     = convex_deployment.prod.name
  domain              = "api.example.com"
  request_destination = "convexCloud"
}

# Fronts the deployment's .convex.site HTTP actions URL. A deployment can have
# one domain per destination, so both can coexist.
resource "convex_custom_domain" "http_actions" {
  deployment_name     = convex_deployment.prod.name
  domain              = "hooks.example.com"
  request_destination = "convexSite"
}

# Convex verifies asynchronously once DNS resolves, so this is false right
# after the first apply and flips to true on a later refresh.
output "api_domain_verified" {
  value = convex_custom_domain.api.verified
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `deployment_name` (String) Name of the deployment the domain points at, such as `playful-otter-123`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `domain` (String) The custom domain itself, for example `api.example.com`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `request_destination` (String) Which endpoint the domain serves. `convexCloud` fronts the deployment's `.convex.cloud` API URL; `convexSite` fronts its `.convex.site` HTTP actions URL. A deployment can have one domain registered for each. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `creation_time` (Number) Creation timestamp, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `verification_time` (Number) Timestamp in milliseconds at which Convex verified the domain, or null while it is still unverified. This is set outside Terraform, once DNS resolves.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether Convex has verified the domain. A convenience for `verification_time != null`; false on a freshly created domain.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Custom domains are imported as
# "<deployment_name>/<request_destination>/<domain>". The destination is part
# of the identity, since the same domain can be registered for both.
terraform import convex_custom_domain.api playful-otter-123/convexCloud/api.example.com
```
